criteria.detail: B75's two published examples, read by this station's closed form rather than by its bisection: example 1 alpha published 1.259921, closed form 1.259921; example 1 beta published 1.259921, closed form 1.259921; example 2 alpha published 1.259921, closed form 1.259921; example 2 beta published 1.000000, closed form 1.000000. **The published value is the outside anchor and the closed form is a different route to it**, so the two can disagree
criteria.name: B94-1

criteria.detail: on 60 of 60 drawn rectangular economies the expansion factor read by B75's bisection equals the largest admissible generalised eigenvalue over square sub-pairs, worst gap 1.18e-07. **So the factor is an eigenvalue after all**, of a square pair `(A_{S,G}, B_{S,G})` rather than of a principal block, which is what B82 registered as missing
criteria.name: B94-2

criteria.detail: the interest factor is the smallest admissible generalised eigenvalue over the same sub-pairs on 60 of 60, worst gap 5.18e-08. **The two factors are the two ends of one finite set**, which is the sharpest form B82's two-families statement takes on a rectangular economy: the families differ in which index set they range over and the factors differ only in the direction the extremum is taken
criteria.name: B94-3

criteria.detail: dropping the feasibility screen and taking the largest generalised eigenvalue over all square sub-pairs overshoots on 54 of 60 economies, by a median factor of 3.565. **A sub-pair's eigenvalue need not be attainable by any non-negative intensity vector on the whole economy**, so the closed form is an extremum over a finite set with a feasibility screen, and saying so is the honest form of the claim: the continuous part is an eigenvalue and the remaining work is a finite search. **The screen does a second job that is easy to miss**: complex generalised eigenvalues turn up on 38 of 60 economies, and keeping their real parts moves the answer on 0 of them, so the filter that drops them is redundant here and the screen is what was rejecting them all along
criteria.name: B94-4

criteria.detail: the block carrying the expansion factor, by size: 1x1 on 28, 2x2 on 15, 3x3 on 10, 4x4 on 5, 5x5 on 2. **More than one size occurs**, so the block is found and not fixed by the shape of the economy. **The single-cell case is the common one**, and there the expansion factor is one process's own output-to-input ratio, chosen by a search rather than computed by one. Printed rather than counted: 3x3 economy -> processes [0, 1, 2], goods [0, 1, 2]; 3x6 economy -> processes [2], goods [0]; 3x5 economy -> processes [0, 2], goods [0, 3]
criteria.name: B94-5

criteria.detail: the number of square sub-pairs visited equals `sum_k C(n,k) C(m,k)` on 60 of 60 economies, median 83 and largest 923. **Everything above is an extremum over that set**, and a set short by one member would make all of it a statement about a different set
criteria.name: B94-6

criteria.detail: B82's file names this station against the registration it opened, so a reader of it finds that the factors are eigenvalues of a block that has to be found. `D20`
criteria.name: B94-7
